customary

KUS-tuh-mair-ee — built on 'custom'; a customary act is simply the usual, accustomed way of doing something. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Customary is according to custom, usual or traditional within a particular community rather than required by any rule.

It is customary in many cultures to remove your shoes before entering someone's home.

Example

At the end of every graduation ceremony at a particular school, the entire senior class tosses their caps into the air at exactly the same moment, a tradition every graduating class has repeated for over fifty years without anyone ever writing it into an official rule.

That long-standing, expected practice everyone simply follows out of tradition is exactly what customary means. Unlike 'mandatory,' which is required by rule, customary is simply what people usually and traditionally do.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

habitual: Habitual means done regularly as one person's habit -- a habitual morning run, a habitual seat in class. Customary belongs to a whole community: people follow the practice because tradition expects it, not because any one individual happens to repeat it.

conventional: Conventional describes doing things the way society at large expects -- the safe, standard choice anywhere you go. Customary points to a particular community's own tradition: a practice can be entirely customary at one school and unheard of everywhere else.

ceremonial: Ceremonial means belonging to a formal ritual's script -- the planned parts of an occasion, printed in the program. Customary practices need no script and no plan; they continue simply because people have always done them.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

rare: happening only seldom

unprecedented: never done or seen before

Where it sits · how deeply rooted in the past — usual → customary → traditional

usual vs. customary: Usual is a more everyday, general word than customary -- usual simply describes what typically happens, while customary specifically emphasizes that a practice is rooted in long-standing tradition.

traditional vs. customary: Traditional can feel even more formal than customary: customary often describes small everyday habits, while traditional usually points to practices passed down across generations.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — custom-

root — custom-: an accustomed way of behaving (Latin (consuetudo, via Old French coustume))

suffix — -ary

suffix — -ary: relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin consuetudo meant 'an accustomed way, a habit,' passed into English through Old French coustume. Customary, at its root, simply relates to whatever people have grown accustomed to doing.

Use the root in a new word: costume

Use the root in a new word: costume: Every actor in the play had to be fitted for an elaborate costume before opening night.
